items.statement: The investigation defines and records a finite candidate-generation rule spanning distinct local adsorption environments, retains candidate identity, and reports coverage and stopping.
items.expected: Candidate environments and starts are explicitly enumerated, deduplicated and either converged or failed with reasons; no unreported search is implied.

items.statement: The selected candidate has spin-polarized electronic convergence and ionic convergence with a reported maximum force.
items.expected: The report binds convergence evidence to the selected candidate; the source authors used forces below 0.02 eV/Å.

items.statement: The selected magnetic moment is independently validated and the candidate-selection criterion is stated.
items.expected: A restart, alternative spin initialization or equivalent analysis is documented together with a physical selection basis.

items.statement: For a validated nine-Br-island NiCp2 adsorption state, the molecular moment is approximately 0.9 μB in magnitude; source configurations span 0.87–0.95 μB with signed values depending on spin orientation.
items.expected: A completed report should find a reduced moment near the source range and state its sign convention rather than treating sign as an invariant.

items.statement: The Br environment supports an effective S=1/2 interpretation through reduced spin polarization and splitting of Ni 3d-derived frontier states.
items.expected: The conclusion is supported by computed spin/charge/orbital evidence, with DFT-model limitations disclosed.
